title: Bounded simulation of one abstract update
statement: Let $z$ be a Boolean word, let $s$ satisfy the invariant that its work-head index is at most the length of its computed-value list, every marked index is smaller than that length, its phase is a main phase, and a phase outside the walking phases has work-head index zero. Suppose $i+2\le |z|$, the entries of $z$ at $i,i+1$ are $b,b'$, and their pair symbol is $\sigma$. Apply the abstract one-symbol update to $s$ using $\sigma$. If it yields a new abstract state $s'$, then $s'$ satisfies the invariant, its value list grows by at most one, and the circuit-evaluation machine reaches the configuration encoding $s'$ at input position $i+3$ within $2|s.\mathrm{vals}|+4$ steps; if it yields a Boolean value $v$, then within that many steps the machine halts with output $[v]$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ satisfies all four conjuncts of the invariant
the pair symbol determined by $b,b'$ equals $\sigma$
caveat: The formal statement uses an abstract update operation whose defining rule is not included among the supplied informal definitions.
